text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 0.45% today to $459.28, continuing a decline that started after hitting $478 six days ago. The broader refining sector faces headwinds despite soaring crude oil prices: while Brent crude has climbed to $116 on Middle East tensions, U.S. refineries are running at 93.4% capacity and gasoline and diesel inventories remain elevated. For a refiner, higher crude input costs paired with high inventory levels can squeeze profit margins, even as the geopolitical premium pushes oil prices higher.

The underlying tension for the stock reflects a mismatch between energy markets and refining economics. U.S. oil sits $7 below Brent crude, and while geopolitical risk is supporting global prices, the domestic refining industry is flush with product inventory—a sign that demand or sales velocity isn't keeping pace with production. In this environment, refiners can struggle to pass soaring input costs to customers quickly enough.
